_: Shared test vectors for fractional order keys.
Checked by BOTH src/fracdex.rs and web/src/lib/fracdex.test.ts. The browser
assigns order keys at typing speed and the API assigns them in batches, so
the two implementations must agree byte for byte — this file is the only
thing that makes a drift fail loudly instead of quietly reordering somebody
null means unbounded: {a: null, b: null} is the first key in an empty ring.
The `between` cases below now include neighbours a peer could send but this
module would never mint. They are the inputs that used to panic the Rust side
(byte slicing, an empty key) or return junk from the TypeScript side; both now
ignore such a neighbour, which is what makes the two agree on hostile input.

between.why: the first key in an empty ring
a wide gap takes the middle digit
and keep growing on the low side
a shared prefix is copied, not decided
below the second digit means a leading zero
a LEADING lowest digit is ordinary
the top digit has no room above it
an empty key is not a key; treated as no neighbour
a trailing lowest digit is refused, not sliced
multi-byte input used to panic the byte slicing
a space is not a digit
